items.stem: What does the District Programs page let you do?

options.text: Maintain the district programs the district offers and link them to the schools that provide them
Create and delete the schools that run each program
Define attendance-area boundaries for each program
Manage staff job assignments for program teachers

items.explanation: The page maintains the district programs offered by the district (and their supplemental data) and provides a link to associate programs with the schools providing them.

misconceptions.b: Schools come from HRAD; SDM can't create or delete them (S3.1).
misconceptions.c: Attendance areas are a separate entity, not part of maintaining a program.
misconceptions.d: Staff job assignments are managed under Staff, not on District Programs.

items.stem: On the District Programs page, what does the link associate?

options.text: Programs to the schools that provide them
Programs to the municipal divisions they serve
Programs to the trustee positions that fund them

items.explanation: The link associates programs to the schools providing them — the same school-program association seen from the Schools page (S3.1).

misconceptions.b: The catalog entry describes a program-to-school link, not program-to-division.
misconceptions.c: Data-owner assignment is a separate access concern, not this link.
misconceptions.d: Trustee positions are unrelated to the program-school link.

items.stem: The district is introducing a new French immersion program and wants three schools to run it. Where do you maintain the program record itself?

options.text: On the District Programs page, then link it to the three schools
On the Schools page, which is where programs are created
Upstream in HRAD, since programs are imported like schools
In the AuditLog, which is the edit surface for new records

items.explanation: The program record is maintained on the District Programs page; you then use the link to associate it with the schools that provide it.

misconceptions.b: The Schools page only links to programs that already exist; it doesn't define the program record.
misconceptions.c: The catalog entry gives no indication programs are imported from HRAD; that fact would be invented.
misconceptions.d: The AuditLog records changes; it isn't an edit surface.

items.stem: A colleague says "I added the immersion program from the Schools page." What's the accurate correction?

options.text: The Schools page links a school to existing programs; the program itself is maintained on District Programs
Both pages create program records, so either is fine
Programs can only be linked, never maintained anywhere in SDM
The Schools page deletes programs; District Programs creates them

items.explanation: From the Schools page you associate a school with District Programs it offers (S3.1); the program record is maintained on the District Programs page and then linked to its providing schools.

misconceptions.b: Only the District Programs page maintains the program record; the Schools page just links.
misconceptions.c: Programs are maintained on the District Programs page — they aren't link-only.
misconceptions.d: Nothing in the source describes the Schools page deleting programs.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, explain what the District Programs page is for and how it relates to the Schools page (S3.1). Use the immersion program as your example.
rubric: States the District Programs page maintains the programs the district offers (and their supplemental data)
States a program is linked/associated to the schools that provide it
Connects to S3.1: the same school-program association is seen from the Schools page, and uses immersion as the example
items.sampleAnswer: The District Programs page is where you maintain the programs the district offers — say a French immersion program — along with their supplemental data, and link each program to the schools that provide it. It's the program's-eye view of the same association you make on the Schools page (S3.1), where a school is connected to the programs it offers.
